content.title: Kimi Antonelli tops Chinese GP qualifying to become F1’s youngest ever pole-sitter
content.text: SHANGHAI, China — Kimi Antonelli became the youngest driver in Formula 1 history to score pole position for a grand prix, as he led qualifying at the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix on Saturday. Antonelli, 19, beat his Mercedes teammate George Russell to pole at the Shanghai International Circuit by two-tenths of a second.Russell, who scored sprint race pole on Friday and won Saturday’s sprint race for Mercedes, had looked set for pole before he was hit by a suspected gearbox problem in the final stage of qualifying that caused his car to briefly stop out on the track. Although Russell was able to get his car going again, he reported on his team radio that he was still struggling to change gear en route back to the pits, where Mercedes changed the steering wheel on his car, as well as several other settings.Russell was sent out at the very end of Q3 to finally set a time in qualifying’s final segment, but he fell 0.222 seconds shy of Antonelli’s leading effort of 1:32.064-seconds. This left Italian driver Antonelli with his maiden F1 pole position.“It was a pretty clean session,” said Antonelli. “(I’m) really happy. A really good session, no mistakes. And (I’m) looking forward to the race tomorrow.”At 19 years, 6 months and 17 days, Antonelli is now the youngest driver in F1 history to score pole position for a grand prix, as his age breaks the previous record held by four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel, who was 21 years, 2 months and 11 days old when he took pole for the 2008 Italian Grand Prix. Vettel went on to score his first GP win the race at Monza the next day.Although Antonelli did top sprint qualifying in Miami last season, when he was 18, this did not officially count in F1’s record books as it was not qualifying for a full grand prix.Speaking after the session, Russell called his second place “damage limitation” after he also suffered a broken front wing in the second part of qualifying, before the suspected gearbox issue struck in Q3.For his late final run, which was completed long after the other nine Q3 runners had completed their last laps, Russell said he had “no (engine) battery, no tire temp, no nothing. (But) the team did a really good job to get into this position. It could have been a lot worse.”Antonelli and Russell will start the race just ahead of Lewis Hamilton, who qualified third for Ferrari, while his teammate Charles Leclerc ended the session in fourth place. Antonelli delivered when it mattered for MercedesAntonelli’s name goes down in F1 history, and it seemed inevitable, given his upward trajectory since joining the grid as a rookie in 2025.“I’m very happy,” Antonelli said, adding, “It’s just the beginning.”As Lewis Hamilton, the seven-time world champion, who was replaced at Mercedes by Antonelli last year, pointed out in the post-qualifying news conference, it’ll be hard for someone to top this record. Drivers usually have to be at least 18 before they can race in F1 and it is rare that such a young driver gets a seat with a top team, such as Mercedes, so early in their grand prix racing career.Antonelli had secured a first sprint pole in Miami last year, in what was just his sixth grand prix event. But a first proper pole position eluded him around Mercedes’ turbulent 2025 campaign.Antonelli endured a roller coaster year himself in 2025, as he endured a rocky stretch through the middle part of the season with a series of poor performances. But he also impressed in securing three top results.Coming into this season, Antonelli has picked up where he left off. Now, though, Mercedes is the consistent frontrunning team.Kimi Antonelli during qualifying at F1’s 2026 Chinese GPAlex Bierens de Haan/Getty ImagesRussell entered this season as the favorite for the drivers’ title, and throughout the Chinese GP weekend to this point that billing held after, after Russell’s victory in Australia last week. The Briton then took the sprint race win earlier on Saturday after battling the Ferraris through the early stages.He looked fast again in the early part of GP qualifying, but when an issue disrupted Russell’s car and compromised his Q3 running, Antonelli stepped up to the plate when it mattered.When asked to share how he improved across the session, given Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc led Q1 and matched Antonelli in Q2, Antonelli revealed he was initially struggling with the balance of his car. But ultimately, he said, “it was nice because for the first time in in a qualifying session, I was able to to find lap time every time I was going on track.”Russell did manage to still qualify second, and Antonelli’s biggest challenges to claim a maiden F1 race win on Sunday are going to be his own teammate, who has seemingly built off of a near-flawless 2025 campaign, and Ferrari.Its pace throughout the weekend has threatened Mercedes and both Hamilton and Leclerc jumped by him after he made another slow start in the sprint to follow the one he made in Melbourne. A good getaway is the minimum he needs to convert pole into victory tomorrow.“They certainly look very strong, especially also on cold tires,” Antonelli said of the Ferraris. “They look like they have good pace. And the start is their very strong point.”Antonelli recognizes the opportunities he has with this mighty Mercedes car but acknowledges that he’s still working on his risk versus reward ratio. Often, drivers get better results when they don’t overdrive and risk mistakes. “It’s about finding the right balance in order to then be able to keep the momentum going,” Antonelli said.This is only his second season, but it’s clear that he’s a rising star that can threaten — and beat — some of the greats on the grid. It’s only a matter of time until he consistently strings performances together as he did in Q3 in Shanghai. – Madeline ColemanResults1 Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes 2 George Russell, Mercedes 3 Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari 4 Charles Leclerc, Ferrari 5 Oscar Piastri, McLaren 6 Lando Norris, McLaren 7 Pierre Gasly, Alpine 8 Max Verstappen, Red Bull 9 Isack Hadjar, Red Bull 10 Ollie Bearman, Haas 11 Nico Hülkenberg, Audi 12 Franco Colapinto, Alpine 13 Esteban Ocon, Haas 14 Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls 15 Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls 16 Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi 17 Carlos Sainz, Williams 18 Alex Albon, Williams 19 Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin 20 Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac 21 Lance Stroll, Aston Martin 22 Sergio Pérez, Cadillac
